fieldMarks: 16-21 in; very like Lesser Scaup but with a more rounded head (high point toward the front) and a larger bill.
In flight shows a longer white wing stripe than Lesser Scaup.
Male head often glosses green (not purple); sides may look whiter.
Females of both scaup may show a pale ear patch in summer.
behavior: Winter flocks on coastal bays may number in the thousands; flocks feeding in tidal current face up-current.
Dives for food; winter diet mainly mussels, clams, oysters and snails; plants, insects and crustaceans in summer.
Migrates in flocks; Alaskan birds may winter on either the Pacific or Atlantic coast.
habitat: Breeds on lakes and bogs near the northern edge of the boreal forest and onto tundra.
Winters mainly on coastal bays, lagoons and estuaries, favoring more open, exposed water than Lesser Scaup; some on inland lakes.
range: Breeds in Alaska and northern Canada and winters along both the Pacific and Atlantic coasts and on some interior lakes of the United States and southern Canada.

lookalikes.name: Lesser scaup
lookalikes.howToTell: Greater has a more rounded head peaking toward the front, a larger bill, a longer white wing stripe, and males often gloss green rather than purple.
